In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of leucocyte and red cell thioguanine metabolite concentrations in patients taking thiopurine drugs.
the measurement and interpretation of intracellular thiopurine metabolite concentrations in the context of the treatment of children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

the development of new methods for the analysis of thioguanine metabolites in erythrocytes and the use of these methods to compare the accumulation of thioguanines in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia taking thioguanine or mercaptopurine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accumulation of erythrocytic TGNs is a more sensitive measure of intracellular TGN accumulation than leucocyte TGM accumulation.
the accumulation of leuco-TGN is similar for both TG and MP in children, but that the accumulation of erythrocytic TGN is significantly higher for TG compared with that for MP.
leucocyte TGT concentrations were not significantly different between the two groups of patients, but that erythrocyte concentrations of TGNs were significantly higher in the TG group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
erythrocyte and leucocyte TGT metabolites should not be used interchangeably for the purpose of monitoring the clinical response to thiopurines.
TG is a more potent thiopurine than MP, but that it has a similar clinical effect in terms of the accumulation of leucoTGNs in children with ALL.

the accumulation of leucoTGN is a better predictor of toxicity in children taking thioguanine, whereas the erythrocyte metabolite accumulation is more predictive of toxicity in children on thioguanine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leucocyte TNG concentrations are not a reliable indicator of thioguanine cytotoxicity, and the measurement of erythrocytes is more appropriate.
the range of leucoTGN concentrations is similar for children taking TG and MP, but erythrocyteTGN metabolite concentrations are significantly higher for those taking TG than for those taking MP.
erythrocyte concentrations should not be used to guide dosing in patients receiving TG, but that leucocyte TNG concentrations should be used.
